posts.title: ¿Qué motivó al representante de la delegación agrícola estadounidense a exclamar "¡increíble!" en una fábrica de productos lácteos vietnamita?
posts.text:
"Increíble" es la frase que Mark Slupek, subdirector del Servicio Agrícola Exterior, utilizó para describir el sistema de producción y logística de la megaplanta láctea de Vinamilk en Vietnam (conocida comúnmente como la Megaplanta). Tras la visita, el representante del USDA comentó que muchos miembros de la delegación también se mostraron sorprendidos por la magnitud y el nivel de automatización de la planta.
La única fábrica de productos lácteos que ha recibido a una delegación agrícola estadounidense .
La visita se realizó en el marco de un programa de promoción del comercio agrícola en Vietnam, que tuvo lugar del 9 al 12 de noviembre y fue liderado por el subsecretario de Agricultura de Estados Unidos, Stephen Alexander Vaden. Según el USDA, esta fue la mayor delegación de promoción comercial que el Servicio Agrícola de Estados Unidos (FAS) haya enviado jamás a Vietnam, con la participación de decenas de empresas, asociaciones industriales y representantes de agencias de gestión agrícola de numerosos estados estadounidenses.
En el programa de trabajo, Vinamilk fue la única fábrica de productos lácteos y una de las tres plantas de producción seleccionadas para la visita. Esta fue también una oportunidad para que los delegados conocieran de primera mano la capacidad de producción de la industria láctea vietnamita y analizaran las oportunidades de cooperación en la cadena de valor agrícola y alimentaria entre ambos países.

posts.title: 加州教師工會籲公立國中小暫停導入 AI 三年
posts.text:
加州教師工會籲公立國中小暫停導入 AI 三年
商傳媒/
[[email protected]](/cdn-cgi/l/email-protection)(編輯中心)
發布：（台灣時間）
資料更新：（台灣時間）
商傳媒｜責任編輯／綜合外電報導
代表加州 12 萬名教職員的教師工會 California Federation of Teachers 日前向加州州長 Gavin Newsom 提出呼籲，要求加州政府實施為期三年的暫緩令，全面暫停在 K-8 公立學校課堂中採用人工智慧（AI）工具。K-8 為美國學制，相當於台灣的幼稚園到國中八年級階段。
工會指出，校園過早引入 AI 存在多重隱憂，包括可能干擾學童大腦發育、缺乏對第一線教育工作者的權益保障，以及學生個人資料外洩的風險。這項訴求源於 Gavin Newsom 先前曾於 2024 年 9 月簽署行政命令，要求加州各州級機構制定 AI 安全規範，而工會希望在相關保障到位前踩煞車。
工會援引麻省理工學院（MIT）與 Wharton Healthcare Analytics Lab 的研究指出，課堂依賴 AI 工具可能削弱學生的腦神經連結並損害學習成效。其中，Wharton Healthcare Analytics Lab 的研究顯示，在沒有任何輔助的數學測驗中，平時使用 GPT-4 的學生測驗成績比完全不使用的同儕低了 17%。
工會主席 Jeff Freitas 在聲明中直言：「學生的腦部發展不應淪為科技巨頭獲利的工具。這是一場公共健康與安全的緊急事件，我們的領導人必須正視並立即採取行動。」加州作為全球科技重鎮，面對 AI 深入義務教育現場展現高度保留態度，也凸顯各界對新科技應用於基礎教育時的倫理與安全審查日益嚴格。

The Cost Difference Between One-Story and Multi-Story Commercial Builds
Commercial buildings in Sherwood Park have changed more in the last decade than the twenty years before. Faster steel-frame erection, tougher energy codes, and weekend-reconfigurable spaces are now expected by owners. Firms stay ahead by handling design, schedule, and long-term operating cost together on every job. Local owners notice the difference when a contractor understands both the soil conditions north of Baseline Road and the city’s permitting quirks. the company site.
A single overlooked fire-separation or HVAC-zoning detail can delay occupancy by months, making team selection critical. The following paragraphs detail how Sherwood Park top Commercial Construction services proceed, today’s realistic price ranges, and checkpoints that differentiate smooth jobs from costly ones.
Understanding Sherwood Park top Commercial Construction services
Projects range from single-tenant retail pads to multi-building industrial campuses. A geotechnical report normally precedes civil drawings that establish parking ratios and stormwater detention. Once permits clear, crews pour foundations designed for Alberta’s freeze-thaw cycles. Steel or engineered-wood framing follows, and mechanical rough-ins are sequenced so that duct runs never compete with sprinkler lines. Inspectors examine vapor barriers, seismic bracing, and emergency egress widths at every stage.
Owners frequently add tenant-improvement packages once the shell is weathertight. These fit-outs can include demountable partitions, upgraded LED lighting, and EV charging stubs. Tenants receive separate pricing for core-and-shell and fit-out from a Sherwood Park top Commercial Construction company so they can distinguish base building from their own customizations. The same firm usually keeps a service division for later Sherwood Park top Commercial Construction repair calls, as a single point of contact speeds warranty work.
Why local experience counts
Concrete placed in winter needs additives and heated enclosures. Summer brings tight crane windows between thunderstorm cells. Crews experienced along Wye Road and Broadmoor Boulevard recognize which ready-mix plants can supply 35 MPa with two-hour notice. Schedule length and change-order exposure are reduced by that same knowledge.
Budget realities and Sherwood Park top Commercial Construction cost ranges
Shell construction for a single-story retail box displays costs of $185 to $245 per square foot in recent municipal filings. Buildings with two office stories and an underground parkade sit near $310 per square foot. Land, soft costs, and tenant fit-out remain outside those figures, which by then cover code-mandated stormwater and fire-protection upgrades. Design fees, permits, and a 5 % contingency now add 18–22 % to Sherwood Park top Commercial Construction prices as steel and lumber volatility lingers.
Faster ROI sometimes leads owners to divide the project into phases. Completing the core and shell first, then leasing the warm shell, allows rental income to reduce the second-phase budget. Pre-construction modeling by a Sherwood Park top Commercial Construction contractor keeps the pro-forma accurate for those cash-flow scenarios.
Sherwood Park top Commercial Construction process starts with clear navigation steps.
A request-for-qualifications issued by owners usually narrows the field to three or four licensed teams. Site walks and reference calls follow. A detailed estimate and a critical-path schedule emerge once a contractor is chosen during the pre-construction phase. Early procurement of long-lead items such as switchgear and curtain-wall extrusions protects the date when the certificate of occupancy can be issued. Weekly superintendent meetings retain trades aligned, and cloud-based document control means every revision is time-stamped for future warranty claims.
The final walkthrough is not a formality. It contains thermal imaging of the roof assembly, airflow readings at each diffuser, and verification that the fire alarm monitoring contract has been activated. Only after those items clear does the project move into the one-year warranty phase that covers both workmanship and equipment begin-up.
Six-step checklist for any Sherwood Park top Commercial Construction project
- Define the program: list square footage, parking count, power density, and future expansion bays before the architect draws the first line. Clear requirements reduce later change orders that average 7 % of contract value on local jobs.
- Secure geotechnical and environmental reports early. Sherwood Park’s glacial till can hide pockets of loose sand that require over-excavation. Knowing this before the bid package is released keeps soil allowances realistic.
- Run a municipal pre-application meeting. Planning staff will flag any arterial road upgrades or off-site levies that affect the Sherwood Park top Commercial Construction cost. Capture those numbers before numbers go to the bank.
- Lock the design at 60 % so the contractor can issue early trade packages. Releasing structural steel drawings while mechanical coordination is still fluid saves eight to ten weeks on most retail projects.
- Establish a shared-document protocol. Every RFI, shop drawing, and inspection report lives in one folder tree. This habit eliminates the “I never saw that revision” disputes that drag warranty close-outs past the contractual deadline.
- Schedule the two-year envelope inspection at the one-year mark. Catching sealant shrinkage or cap flashing movement early keeps water out of the wall cavity and protects finishes that tenants have already installed.
Practical Sherwood Park top Commercial Construction tips from recent local projects
Ask every bidder for a line-item schedule of values that matches the critical path. You can see immediately which downstream trades require re-sequencing instead of arguing over a single delay claim at the end when a concrete pour slips three weeks.. their home page.
- Request thermal-break details on every canopy and parapet; the incremental cost is small, but heating-load calculations drop enough to shrink the rooftop unit by one ton.
- Pre-order the main electrical switchboard the same week the building permit is issued. Lead times still hover near 26 weeks, and a missing 800-amp panel can push revenue recognition an entire quarter.
- Specify LED high-bay fixtures with field-replaceable drivers. Re-lamping a 24-foot warehouse aisle later costs more in lifts and lost production than the upgrade does at install.
- Include a 10 % snow-load factor on all roof steel even if code minimums are lower. The extra stiffness lets future tenants hang mezzanines without reinforcing the whole structure.
- Retain a 3 % cash allowance for municipal inspection re-checks. Sherwood Park’s building department regularly requires a second visit for fire-sprinkler flow tests, and the allowance prevents last-minute invoice disputes.
Frequently asked questions
What is Sherwood Park top Commercial Construction?
It covers the full cycle of designing, permitting, and building retail, office, and light-industrial properties inside Sherwood Park’s municipal boundaries. The work contains site grading, structural frames, mechanical and electrical systems, and the interior partitions that turn an empty shell into usable square footage for a tenant.
How do I choose a Sherwood Park top Commercial Construction provider?
Begin with a shortlist of firms that hold a current City of Sherwood Park business license and carry at least five million dollars in liability coverage. Ask each to supply three recent references for projects of similar size and occupancy type. Then compare proposed schedules and the percentage of work they self-perform versus subcontract. The team that can show both a detailed Gantt chart and a superintendent who has run three comparable jobs in the last two years usually delivers the fewest surprises.
How much does Sherwood Park top Commercial Construction cost?
Current bids show single-story retail shells between one hundred eighty-five and two hundred forty-five dollars per square foot. Two-story offices with structured parking run closer to three hundred ten dollars per square foot. Add eighteen to twenty-two percent for design, permits, and contingency. These figures assume 2024 material prices and normal winter weather windows; unusual soil conditions or accelerated schedules can push the envelope higher.
How long does a typical Sherwood Park top Commercial Construction project take?
From signed contract to certificate of occupancy, a 15,000-square-foot retail building usually needs nine to eleven months. That window includes four weeks for civil approvals, three weeks of foundation curing in winter, and two weeks for final inspections. Larger phased campuses stretch to fourteen months as civil works and building construction run in parallel.
What permits does Sherwood Park top Commercial Construction require?
A development permit, building permit, and trade permits for electrical, mechanical, and plumbing are mandatory. An extra access permit from Strathcona County may apply if the site borders an arterial road. Environmental permits surface when the parcel sits on a former service-station or dry-cleaning location.
Can an existing building be upgraded under Sherwood Park top Commercial Construction services?
Yes. Several owners choose seismic, energy-code, and accessibility upgrades rather than recent construction. A Sherwood Park top Commercial Construction contractor can perform a facility condition assessment, then phase the work so tenants stay in place. Typical packages include new HVAC controls, LED retrofits, and vestibule additions that cut energy use 20–25 % without touching the structural frame.
Clear scope documents, realistic schedules, and a contractor who previously knows the local inspection staff retain most Sherwood Park commercial projects on budget. The same habits protect long-term operating costs once the building opens.
Owners who treat the process as a sequence of informed decisions rather than a single price comparison tend to occupy finished space sooner and with fewer warranty calls later. their website.

posts.title: Pottsville, Schuylkill Technology Center Partnership to Restore Blighted Property and Employ Students
posts.text:
POTTSVILLE — A new partnership between the Pottsville Redevelopment Authority and Schuylkill Technology Center aims to return a blighted building to productive use while giving local students paid, hands-on experience in the building trades.
The initiative was announced during the city’s Veterans Day press conference on , which Skook News previously covered in a report on Pottsville’s redevelopment efforts, grants and city improvements.
How the Redevelopment Partnership Will Work
The initiative was spearheaded by Councilman Andy Wollyung and is being administered through the Redevelopment Authority under Chairman Bud Quandel. It is part of a broader redevelopment effort supported by a $1.5 million grant from the Pennsylvania Department of Community and Economic Development.
According to the city, the Redevelopment Authority and STC are working together to identify and acquire a vacant, blighted property for the project. A private developer would rehabilitate the building while employing STC students.
During the press conference, Quandel explained that the authority would acquire the building, pay closing costs and provide up to $20,000 toward engineering, design and permit costs. The selected developer would finance the remainder of the rehabilitation.
Quandel said a public Request for Proposals would be issued after legal review is completed. According to the city’s announcement, the authority will invite developers to submit rehabilitation plans once the property is acquired. The proposal period will remain open for 45 days and include two public walk-throughs of the building, along with an opportunity to submit questions.
Requirements for Developer Proposals
Developers must provide a business plan outlining how they would take the property from its current condition to a verified Certificate of Occupancy from the City of Pottsville.
Each proposal must also include:
- At least 1,000 hours of cooperative work for STC students.
- Proof of insurance.
- The ability to hire students.
- A total rehabilitation cost estimate.
After the Certificate of Occupancy is issued and the required student work hours are verified, the developer will receive the property from the authority at no cost.
“Blighted buildings hold back our neighborhoods, and this partnership gives us a new way to deal with them,” Mayor Tom Smith said. “We’re bringing together the Redevelopment Authority, STC, and a private developer to put a building back to use, and we’re training the next generation of Pottsville’s workforce while we do it.”
Paid Work Experience for STC Students
Students will be employees of the selected developer and work under the developer’s on-site supervision and required insurance coverage.
STC Cooperative Education & Diversified Occupations Coordinator TJ Fitzpatrick will provide general supervision and meet weekly with the developer to review progress and ensure students’ work meets expectations.
“Our students train in the classroom and the shop, and a project like this lets them take those skills onto a real job site, working alongside experienced professionals and earning a paycheck,” said Shannon Brennan, STC’s assistant executive director and director of career and technical education.
“Experiences like this help students see where their training can take them, and they strengthen the local workforce,” Brennan added.
Redevelopment Authority Chairman Bud Quandel said the initiative would benefit both the community and students preparing to enter the workforce.
“This program is about turning a liability into an asset for the community,” Quandel said. “A developer who takes on this project will have a clear path to completion, and students will gain real experience on a building in their own backyard. We look forward to seeing the proposals we receive.”
Property Announcement and Developer Inquiries
The property address and proposal timeline will be announced after the acquisition is completed.
Developers and community members who want to be notified when the Request for Proposals is released can contact City Administrator Rob Straebel at (570) 622-1234 or cityadministrator@pottsvillepa.gov.

posts.title: Kazakhstan unveils over 32 billion tenge in green projects at COP31
posts.text:
Kazakhstan unveils over 32 billion tenge in green projects at COP31
Kazakhstan presented two green investment projects worth a combined 32.42 billion tenge at the COP31 UN Climate Change Conference in Antalya, Türkiye, a Qazinform News Agency correspondent reports.
The initiatives, unveiled at Kazakhstan's national pavilion during a session titled "Kazakhstan's Carbon Market: From National Mechanisms to International Cooperation," involve the construction of a lithium-ion battery recycling facility and a 70-megawatt solar power plant in Almaty region.
The first project, Nuloop Kazakhstan, involves building a facility in the Kairat industrial zone to collect and recycle used lithium-ion batteries. With an investment of 11.95 billion tenge, the plant will recover valuable materials from spent batteries, help reduce hazardous waste, and introduce modern recycling technologies.
The facility is also expected to create new jobs and support the growth of Kazakhstan's recycling industry.
The second project, led by LoopEnerGren Capital, involves the construction of a 70 MW solar power plant at an estimated cost of 20.47 billion tenge. Once completed, the plant is expected to boost renewable energy production, cut greenhouse gas emissions, and strengthen the region's energy infrastructure.
Both initiatives are being supported by the International Green Technologies and Investment Projects Center (IGTIC), in cooperation with the Investment Committee of Kazakhstan's Ministry of Foreign Affairs.
The presentation of these projects at COP31 highlights Kazakhstan's efforts to turn its climate commitments into concrete investment opportunities and environmental initiatives.
Opening the session, Kazakhstan's Minister of Ecology and Natural Resources, Alibek Kuantyrov, noted that the country's national emissions trading system has been in place since 2013.
He said Kazakhstan is now working to develop a unified carbon market framework that would bring together its existing emissions trading system, voluntary carbon market mechanisms, and international cooperation under Article 6 of the Paris Agreement.
Kuantyrov also emphasized the need for transparent monitoring, reporting, and verification, noting that reliable carbon credits and compliance with international standards are essential for attracting foreign partners and investment in climate projects.
IGTIC Chairman Saken Kalkamanov presented the center as a one-stop platform for international investors seeking opportunities in Kazakhstan's climate and carbon markets.
He outlined its work in supporting projects under Article 6 of the Paris Agreement, maintaining the Green Technologies and Projects Registry, and developing the Kazakhstan Country Climate Investment Platform (QCIP).
The event also featured the signing of a memorandum of understanding between Kazakhstan's Atameken National Chamber of Entrepreneurs and the Turkish Industry and Business Association (TÜSİAD), along with an agreement between Zhasyl Damu JSC and international partners.
The agreements are intended to strengthen business ties and expand cooperation on climate policy and carbon market development.
During the session, participants discussed international transfers of carbon credits, the implementation of Article 6 mechanisms, the expansion of voluntary carbon markets, and ways to attract private investment into environmental projects.
Representatives of NULOOP also submitted recommendations to Kazakhstan's Ministry of Ecology and Natural Resources on developing a nationwide system for collecting and recycling used lithium-ion batteries.
Kazakhstan's participation in COP31 highlights its efforts to turn climate commitments into investment opportunities. The two projects, worth more than 32 billion tenge, are expected to support the growth of renewable energy and the circular economy, while expanding international partnerships could help attract additional capital and introduce advanced environmental technologies.
Earlier, Qazinform reported that Kazakhstan signed $1.2 billion in agreements at COP31 in Antalya.

Kuantyrov also emphasized the need for transparent monitoring, reporting, and verification, noting that reliable carbon credits and compliance with international standards are essential for attracting foreign partners and investment in climate projects. IGTIC Chairman Saken Kalkamanov presented the center as a one-stop platform for international investors seeking opportunities in Kazakhstan's climate and carbon markets.

posts.title: L'Allemagne risque-t‑elle un hiver rigoureux? La ministre de l'Économie Reiche mise en urgence sur les centrales au charbon et au fioul
posts.text:
La ministre allemande de l’Économie, Katherina Reiche (CDU), veut, au moyen d’une loi d’urgence, rendre d’anciennes centrales au charbon et au fioul à nouveau réactivables pour l’hiver. En toile de fond se trouvent des réserves de gaz inhabituellement basses. Auparavant, son ministère avait renoncé pendant des mois à des mesures de précaution supplémentaires.
Comme le rapporte le Spiegel, se référant à un projet de loi daté du 16 octobre, des centrales mises à l’arrêt devraient être autorisées à injecter de nouveau de l’électricité dans le réseau en cas de pénurie de gaz menaçante. Les installations se trouvent dans ce que l’on appelle une réserve froide: elles sont hors service, mais doivent rester disponibles pour les situations d’urgence.
La loi doit déjà s’appliquer au niveau d’alerte dit « d’alarme ». Il s’agit du deuxième des trois niveaux d’alerte pour l’approvisionnement en gaz, déclenché lorsqu’une pénurie de gaz menace. Les centrales mises à l’arrêt pourraient alors à nouveau produire de l’électricité afin d’économiser le gaz naturel. La réglementation doit entrer en vigueur dès cet hiver et expirer fin mars 2028.
Le ministère justifie ces plans d’urgence par la guerre en Iran, qui pèse sur les marchés gaziers internationaux et accroît le risque de goulets d’étranglement dans l’approvisionnement. Cependant, la guerre dure déjà depuis fin février. Malgré cela, Reiche n’a, selon le Spiegel, longtemps pris aucune mesure supplémentaire en vue de l’hiver.
Les conséquences se manifestent dans les réserves de gaz: au 1er novembre, les stocks allemands n’étaient remplis qu’à 61 %, un niveau jamais atteint à cette date depuis le début de relevés comparables. En raison des prix élevés en été, les entreprises avaient stocké peu de gaz. Reiche comptait sur le fait que le marché garantirait l’approvisionnement. Ce n’est que tardivement qu’elle a chargé l’entreprise publique Sefe de procéder à des injections supplémentaires. Celles‑ci n’ont toutefois relevé le niveau de remplissage que de façon marginale.
Une loi similaire avait déjà été introduite en 2022 par le prédécesseur de Reiche, Robert Habeck. Des critiques issus du secteur de l’énergie mettent en garde contre le risque qu’une activation trop précoce de la réserve ne fausse les prix de l’électricité. Le responsable politique écologiste Michael Kellner reproche en outre à Reiche d’avoir manqué le remplissage en temps voulu des réserves de gaz.
